title: Sichuan Chili Oil (Erjingtiao & Facing Heaven)
headnote: DRAFT / UNTESTED FINAL BUILD. Recovered April 21, 2026 authentic-leaning chili oil with Erjingtiao and Facing Heaven chilies, whole-spice oil infusion, a three-stage oil pour, and subtle rock-sugar sweetness. User liked a prior Mala Market version but wanted more sweetness; no tasting result for this custom version was found.

ingredientGroups.title: Chili bowl
items: ¾ cup Erjingtiao chili flakes (weigh after crushing; weight was not recorded)
¼ cup Facing Heaven chili flakes (weight was not recorded)
2 tsp crushed rock sugar (small crystals are suitable)

ingredientGroups.title: Infused oil
items: 2 cups neutral oil (approximately 440 g; varies by oil)

steps: Place all ingredients for the chili bowl into a dry, large, heatproof bowl with ample room to accommodate hot oil; stir to combine.

Add oil, garlic, shallot, ginger, scallions, and the whole spices to a pot. Gradually heat the oil to 250–275°F and hold approximately 12–15 minutes, allowing the aromatics to gently sizzle and become fragrant without scorching.
Strain out all solids and return the infused oil to the pot. Heat to around 350°F, monitoring closely with a thermometer; do not leave the hot oil unattended.
Carefully pour roughly one-third of the hot oil over the chili mixture at about 350°F. The chilies should bubble and bloom, not turn black. Keep face and hands back from steam and splatter.
Allow the remaining oil to cool to roughly 300°F, about 20–30 seconds or as indicated by your thermometer, then pour another third over the chilies.
When the remaining oil cools to around 250°F, pour the last third over the bowl and stir gently.

Let rest at least 30–60 minutes; flavor develops best over 24–48 hours. Cool fully and refrigerate in a clean airtight container; use promptly and avoid storing homemade garlic-infused chili oil at room temperature.
